title: The Contact of Vienna
premise: Zephyrine Montrose, an interpreter for a fractious Vienna peace delegation, discovers their own voiceprint is the biometric key to a black-site server in Singapore — evidence that a shadowy training network has been scripting negotiators, including Zephyrine, for a decade. As the delegation's talks collapse on schedule, Zephyrine and disgraced analyst Tomas Reiner race across three checkpoints to expose the network, torn between loyalty to the mentor who built them and the truth that will destroy her. In the end, Zephyrine burns the server with their own voice, sacrifices the treaty, and walks out of Vienna stateless but free, carrying the only uncorrupted copy of the truth.
about_author: Ada Nakamura is a former conference interpreter who spent a decade in Geneva before turning to fiction full-time. Her thrillers are known for their linguistic precision and their fascination with the people who stand between languages — and between lies.

chapters.title: Simultaneous
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Opening at the Vienna peace talks, Zephyrine renders a delegate's insult flawlessly and realizes mid-sentence they are translating words they were trained to expect. The beat: unease disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Rewrite
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Reviewing the delegation's revised protocol, Zephyrine notices the rule changes mirror phrases from their old training academy in Lyon. A call from mentor Hélène Vasseur reassures — too smoothly. Beat: first crack in trust.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Tomas Reiner's POV. In a Vienna data annex, analyst Tomas discovers an authentication request from a Singapore server awaiting one key: Zephyrine Montrose's voice. He flags it and is ordered to bury it. Beat: reluctant curiosity hardening into defiance.

chapters.title: Café Sperl, 9 P.M.
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Tomas approaches Zephyrine with the flag; Zephyrine initially reports him to delegation security, then replays the conversation all night. Beat: the choice between duty and doubt made at 3 a.m.

chapters.title: What Lyon Taught
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Flashback interwoven with present: twelve years ago at the academy, Hélène drilled not language but judgment — which concessions to soften, which lies to smooth. Zephyrine tests a memory against the server metadata. Beat: grief.

chapters.title: The Delegation That Fails
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The talks derail exactly on the schedule hidden in the Singapore server's cached files. Tomas realizes the collapse isn't incompetence; it's choreography. Beat: cold horror.

chapters.title: Hélène
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Confrontation with Hélène, who neither confirms nor denies but warns Zephyrine to take a posting in Montevideo and forget Vienna. She says 'you were my best work.' Beat: love weaponized.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: Schwechat
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Tomas, now officially fugitives, try to leave Austria with a copied authentication token and are nearly caught by delegation security chief Brandt. Beat: adrenaline and the first real betrayal of their badges.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A dead-drop package from Hélène contains the academy's original charter — and a personal letter revealing Hélène was trained the same way, a link in a chain decades long. Beat: pity complicating anger.

chapters.title: Istanbul Layover
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. In Istanbul the pair decodes the server's directory: 300 interpreters, diplomats, and mediators worldwide, all 'tuned' by the network. One name is flagged for deletion this week. Beat: the stakes turn personal and global at once.

chapters.title: The Flagged Name
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The deletion target is Amara Diallo, a mediator in Nairobi and Zephyrine's only true friend from the academy. A warning call is intercepted; the network knows they're moving. Beat: loyalty as a liability.

chapters.title: Brandt's Offer
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Security chief Brandt corners them in a hotel lobby: come home, testify to nothing, and Zephyrine keeps their career and Hélène's freedom. Zephyrine refuses; Tomas wavers. Beat: the cost of truth priced in a person.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: Nairobi
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Reaching Amara, Zephyrine finds her already half-erased — identity documents dissolved, accounts frozen. Amara chooses to help anyway, giving them her old diplomatic courier access. Beat: friendship as resistance.

chapters.title: The Training Floor
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Inside a decommissioned Nairobi relay station, Tomas finds the network's local node: recordings of Zephyrine's own sessions, annotated with behavioral corrections. He doesn't tell Zephyrine how bad the annotations are. Beat: protective deception.

chapters.title: What Tomas Didn't Say
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine finds the annotations anyway — including notes that Tomas's own recruitment was engineered to keep them compliant. Confrontation; the alliance fractures on the eve of the endgame. Beat: heartbreak.

chapters.title: Hélène's Confession
chapters.summary: Hélène's POV, one chapter only. In Vienna, Hélène meets the network's director, buys Zephyrine twelve hours by feeding false coordinates, and records a full confession addressed to Zephyrine. Beat: a mentor's love expressed as sacrifice.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: Singapore
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Tomas, reconciled but raw, enter the data center district as border shifts change in four hours. Brandt's team is close behind, and so is the network's cleanup crew. Beat: ticking clock fully armed.

chapters.title: The Server Room
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The vault accepts Zephyrine's voice — and plays Hélène's confession through its own speakers: the network is listening, always. Zephyrine must choose between copying the archive or destroying it. Beat: the thematic crux.

chapters.title: Burn the Network
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They do both: stream the archive to a hundred journalists as the thermite charge Tomas planted takes the servers. The cleanup crew arrives to ash and a spreading headline. Beat: catharsis through fire.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The escape through the checkpoint as shifts turn — Brandt, ordered now to bury the scandal instead, lets them pass with a nod. Beat: bitter mercy.

chapters.title: Stateless
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Vienna, one month later. The treaty is dead, the delegation dissolved, Hélène in custody, Zephyrine's credentials revoked. Reading Hélène's letter one last time, Zephyrine burns it too. Beat: mourning without regret.

chapters.title: Interpreting Silence
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, epilogue. In a small Lisbon language school, Zephyrine teaches refugees to find their own words, unscripted. A student asks what the best interpreters are made of. Zephyrine answers: 'Someone who chooses what they mean.' Beat: quiet, earned freedom.
